what.title: What MAPLE is
what.body: Democracy works best when residents and their representatives can actually hear each other. MAPLE is a free, open-source, nonpartisan platform where anyone can read and submit testimony on bills before the Massachusetts Legislature, and follow what happens next.

why.title: Why we're asking
paragraphs: Infrastructure like this is hard to fund. It doesn't take sides, so no side pays for it. It isn't flashy, so it rarely makes headlines. And no single interest owns it, which is exactly the point.
That's why everyone who values it has to chip in. A broad base of supporters, from across the political spectrum, is also the best proof that MAPLE belongs to the public.

funds.title: What your gift funds
funds.body: The Legislature's new two-year session begins in January 2027. Gifts to the challenge pay for MAPLE's work through that session.

items.title: Keeping MAPLE free and running
items.body: Hosting, maintenance and support for everyone who uses it.

items.title: Clearer legislative information
items.body: Planned legislator and committee profiles, and a bill page that brings testimony, lobbying, votes and campaign finance together.

items.title: Tools for civic organizations
items.body: Planned features that help groups engage members in testimony and follow the bills and legislators they care about.

items.title: Coalition building
items.body: Working groups with civic organizations, journalists and legislative staff that shape what MAPLE builds next.

levels.title: Ways to give

items.body: A gift from someone who has testified, or wants to.
A strong vote of confidence in public legislative infrastructure.
A leadership gift. Can be pledged over time.

sustainer.body: For individuals and foundations who want to help carry MAPLE's core costs year-round.

items.q: Has the funder already given the $125,000?
items.a: Yes. Their grant is already committed to MAPLE, whether or not we reach the goal. They challenged the community to raise $125,000 more. Your gift doesn't unlock their money; it shows that the people who use and value MAPLE will help sustain it.

items.q: What happens if we don't reach $125,000?
items.a: Every gift still goes to MAPLE's work this session. Reaching the goal is the strongest signal we can send to other funders that this infrastructure has public support.
To Partners in Democracy, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, restricted to MAPLE. Gifts are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law, and gifts of $250 or more receive a written acknowledgment.
MAPLE does not take positions on legislation, and anyone can testify for or against any bill. [Link to MAPLE's governance statement once published.]
